entry.name: seq~
entry.description: The seq~ object is an event sequencer that is driven by a signal input. seq~ can be used to create looping sequences of control data that are synchronized to a phasor~.

messages.digest: The word, followed by an int, a float and a message, inserts a Max event specified by the message at the time specified by the float for the sequence number specified by the int. (e.g.,will insert the messageto be played at the halfway point of sequence 2.)

messages.argPattern: sequence-name (symbol), start time (float), optional end time (float) and Max-Event (message):list

messages.name: anything
messages.digest: Theobject is used to record and play back messages.
messages.description: Theobject is used to record and play back messages. All events received in the inlet are stored according to the current value of the input signal. Any message can be sequenced except for commands to theobject itself. The example shows a simple way to work around this limitation.Note:can be used to sequence MIDI data if the MIDI input stream is converted into lists of MIDI events. This conversion is necessary to avoid outputting a corrupted MIDI stream which would occur if only the raw int messages of a MIDI stream were sequenced individually and theobject were not doing a simple forward linear playback.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Causes information about theobject's current sequence number, mode of operation (record, overdub, play)
messages.description: Causes information about theobject's current sequence number, mode of operation (record, overdub, play) and total number of current events to be printed in the Max window.

messages.name: clear
messages.digest: The word, followed by the name of a sequence, erases the sequence.
messages.description: The word, followed by the name of a sequence, erases the sequence. The messageerases all current sequences.

messages.name: delete
messages.digest: The word, followed by an symbol that specifies a sequence name, a float and a message, deletes a Max event or events specified by the message at the time specified by the float for the sequence name specified by the symbol. An additional end time may also be specified. Here are some examples:: delete all the events at time 5 in mysequence.: delete all the events between time 6.5 and 8 in mysequence.: delete only the event explosion wherever it occurs.

messages.name: overdub
messages.digest: The word, followed by 1, causesto begin Max event recording of the current sequence (set by themessage)
messages.description: The word, followed by 1, causesto begin Max event recording of the current sequence (set by themessage) in "overdub" mode. Recording begins at the current point of the loop and wraps around at the point where the input signal reaches 1, continuing to record as the signal passes its original value. The messageturns off overdub mode.

messages.name: play
messages.digest: The word, followed by 1, causesto begin Max event playback of the current sequence (set by themessage)
messages.description: The word, followed by 1, causesto begin Max event playback of the current sequence (set by themessage) at the point of the loop specified by the current value of the signal input.turns off playback. By default, playback is off.

messages.description: Reads a text file containing Max event sequences created using theobject'smessage into the memory of the.object. If no symbol argument appears after the word, a standard open file dialog is opened showing available text files. The word, followed by a symbol, reads the file whose filename corresponds to the symbol into theobject's memory without opening the dialog box.

messages.digest: Saves the contents of all current Max event sequences into a text file.
messages.description: Saves the contents of all current Max event sequences into a text file. A standard file dialog is opened for naming the file.
